osces.title: Hypertensive Emergency - Suspected Aortic Dissection

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Sudden onset severe chest pain radiating to back for 2 hours
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Patient presents with sudden-onset severe tearing chest pain that started 2 hours ago while lifting heavy equipment at work. Pain is 10/10 severity, tearing in quality, radiating through to the interscapular region. Associated with diaphoresis and mild dyspnoea. No syncope. Pain different from his usual angina. Previously well-controlled hypertension, but admits to stopping medications 3 weeks ago due to side effects.

social_history.occupation_detail: Construction foreman, heavy lifting daily, high stress environment

patient_scenario.family_history: Father died of myocardial infarction age 62, mother has hypertension, brother had aortic aneurysm repair age 55

vital_signs.blood_pressure: Right arm 186/108 mmHg, Left arm 154/92 mmHg

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP not elevated, dual heart sounds with soft early diastolic murmur at left sternal edge, peripheral pulses asymmetric with diminished left radial pulse, no peripheral oedema
examination_findings.respiratory: Clear lung fields bilaterally, no crackles or wheeze, equal air entry
examination_findings.other_systems: Abdomen soft, non-tender, no pulsatile mass. Neurologically intact, no focal deficits

investigations.ecg: Sinus tachycardia 102 bpm, left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage criteria (SV1 + RV5 = 42mm), no acute ST segment changes, PR interval 160ms, QRS 98ms, QTc 440ms
investigations.chest_xray: Widened mediastinum measuring 9.2cm at aortic knob level, clear lung fields, normal cardiac size, no pleural effusion
investigations.bloods: Troponin I 18 ng/L (normal <26), D-dimer 1850 ng/mL (normal <500), Creatinine 98 μmol/L, eGFR 72 mL/min/1.73m², Na 138 mmol/L, K 4.2 mmol/L, Hb 142 g/L, WCC 11.2 x10⁹/L

immediate: IV labetalol 20mg bolus, then infusion 1-2mg/min titrated to SBP 100-120mmHg and HR <60bpm
IV morphine 2.5-5mg for analgesia
Urgent CT aortic angiogram with contrast
Cardiothoracic surgery consultation
Type and cross-match 6 units packed red cells
short_term: Transfer to CCU for continuous BP monitoring
Maintain SBP 100-120mmHg with IV antihypertensives
Serial ECGs and cardiac enzymes
Transoesophageal echo if CT inconclusive
long_term: Definitive surgical management if Type A dissection confirmed
Medical management if Type B dissection
Lifelong antihypertensive therapy
Surveillance imaging of aorta
Cardiac rehabilitation program
discharge_planning: Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous exercise

marking_criteria.item: Measures blood pressure in both arms
Recognises BP differential >20mmHg as red flag
Identifies tearing pain radiating to back as dissection feature
Notes widened mediastinum on chest X-ray
Initiates IV beta-blocker for BP and shear stress control

learning_objectives: Recognise clinical features of aortic dissection per eTG Cardiovascular
Perform bilateral BP measurement to detect dissection-related differential
Initiate appropriate anti-impulse therapy with IV beta-blockade per CSANZ guidelines
Order appropriate urgent imaging for aortic pathology
references: CSANZ Position Statement on Acute Aortic Syndromes 2021
National Heart Foundation: Hypertensive emergencies guideline 2016

osces.title: Decompensated Heart Failure - Diuretic Optimisation

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Progressive dyspnoea and leg swelling over 5 days
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Presents with 5-day history of progressive exertional dyspnoea, now breathless after 20 metres (usually walks 500m). Orthopnoea requiring 3 pillows (usually 1). Two episodes of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea. Bilateral ankle swelling extending to mid-shin. Weight gain of 4kg over past week. Compliant with medications but ran out of frusemide 10 days ago. No chest pain, palpitations or syncope.

social_history.occupation_detail: Retired teacher, lives alone in single-storey house, daughter visits daily

patient_scenario.family_history: Mother had heart failure, father had stroke age 78

examination_findings.cardiovascular: JVP elevated to 8cm above sternal angle, irregularly irregular pulse, displaced apex beat 6th intercostal space anterior axillary line, soft pansystolic murmur at apex, bilateral pitting oedema to knees
examination_findings.respiratory: Bibasal fine inspiratory crackles to mid-zones, dullness to percussion at both bases
examination_findings.other_systems: Abdomen soft with mild hepatomegaly 2cm below costal margin, no ascites

investigations.ecg: Atrial fibrillation with ventricular rate 88 bpm, left bundle branch block pattern, QRS duration 140ms
investigations.chest_xray: Cardiomegaly with cardiothoracic ratio 0.58, upper lobe blood diversion, Kerley B lines, bilateral pleural effusions
investigations.bloods: BNP 1850 pg/mL (normal <100), Troponin I 42 ng/L (baseline 35), Creatinine 125 μmol/L (baseline 95), eGFR 42 mL/min/1.73m², Na 134 mmol/L, K 4.8 mmol/L, Urea 12.2 mmol/L, Hb 108 g/L, Albumin 32 g/L
investigations.echocardiogram: Previous echo (6 months ago): LVEF 35%, moderate MR, dilated LA, RVSP 45mmHg
investigations.other: Daily weight chart shows 4kg gain over 5 days

immediate: IV frusemide 80mg stat (double usual oral dose per eTG)
Oxygen 2-4L/min via nasal prongs to maintain SpO2 >94%
Fluid restriction 1.5L/day
Daily weights same time each morning
Strict fluid balance chart
short_term: IV frusemide 40mg BD for 48 hours
Monitor UEC daily while on IV diuretics
Target weight loss 0.5-1kg/day
Consider metolazone 2.5mg if inadequate diuresis
Cardiac monitoring for arrhythmias
long_term: Optimise oral frusemide dose before discharge (likely 80mg daily)
Continue guideline-directed medical therapy
Heart failure nurse education program
Consider cardiac resynchronisation therapy given LBBB
Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination
discharge_planning: Daily weights with action plan if >2kg gain
Heart failure clinic follow-up in 1 week
GP review in 3 days for UEC check

marking_criteria.item: Assesses volume status with JVP examination
Reviews weight chart for fluid gain
Calculates appropriate IV frusemide dose (2x oral dose)
Provides patient education on fluid management

learning_objectives: Assess volume status in decompensated heart failure per eTG Cardiovascular
Calculate appropriate IV diuretic dosing for acute decompensation
Monitor for diuretic-related complications including electrolyte disturbance and renal dysfunction
Implement comprehensive heart failure management per CSANZ Heart Failure Guidelines
references: eTG - Cardiovascular: Acute heart failure management
National Heart Foundation: Living Well with Heart Failure 2022

osces.title: Atrial Fibrillation - Rate Control and Anticoagulation

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Palpitations and reduced exercise tolerance for 3 weeks
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Three-week history of intermittent palpitations, describes heart 'racing and irregular'. Episodes last hours to days. Associated with mild dyspnoea on exertion and fatigue. Can now only walk 200m before breathlessness (previously unlimited). No chest pain, syncope or presyncope. Noticed irregular pulse when checking blood pressure at home. First episode of these symptoms.
past_medical_history: Obstructive sleep apnoea on CPAP since 2019

social_history.alcohol: 20 standard drinks per week (wine with meals)
social_history.occupation_detail: Owns busy Italian restaurant, works 60 hours/week, high stress

patient_scenario.family_history: Father had stroke age 72, mother has AF diagnosed age 75

examination_findings.cardiovascular: Irregularly irregular pulse with variable intensity S1, JVP not elevated, no murmurs, no peripheral oedema
examination_findings.respiratory: Clear lung fields, no crackles or wheeze
examination_findings.other_systems: Abdomen soft, obese (BMI 31), no organomegaly. No focal neurological deficits

investigations.ecg: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response 118 bpm, no evidence of pre-excitation, normal QRS morphology, QRS duration 92ms, no acute ST-T changes
investigations.chest_xray: Normal cardiac size, clear lung fields, no pulmonary congestion
investigations.bloods: TSH 2.8 mIU/L (normal 0.5-4.0), Creatinine 92 μmol/L, eGFR 78 mL/min/1.73m², Na 139 mmol/L, K 4.3 mmol/L, Mg 0.92 mmol/L, HbA1c 7.2%, LDL 3.1 mmol/L
investigations.echocardiogram: Moderate left atrial enlargement (LA volume 38mL/m²), normal LV systolic function (LVEF 60%), mild MR, no LVH
investigations.other: 24-hour Holter (if performed) would show persistent AF

immediate: Metoprolol 50mg BD for rate control (PBS 2933E)
Calculate CHA₂DS₂-VASc score = 4 (Age 1, HTN 1, DM 1, Vascular 1)
Calculate HAS-BLED score = 2 (HTN 1, Alcohol 1)
Start rivaroxaban 20mg daily with dinner (PBS 10294N - requires authority)
ECG to confirm rate control achieved (<110 bpm at rest)
short_term: Titrate metoprolol to achieve resting HR <110 bpm
Baseline LFTs and renal function before anticoagulation
Consider rhythm control if symptoms persist despite rate control
Reduce alcohol intake to <10 standard drinks/week
Sleep study review to ensure CPAP compliance
long_term: Annual stroke and bleeding risk reassessment
Consider catheter ablation if rate control inadequate
Optimise cardiovascular risk factors
Regular INR not required with rivaroxaban
Annual echocardiogram to monitor LA size
discharge_planning: Metoprolol 50mg BD (increase to 100mg BD if needed)
GP review in 1 week for rate control assessment

marking_criteria.item: Chooses appropriate anticoagulant with correct dose
Sets appropriate rate control target (<110 bpm)
Considers rhythm vs rate control strategy
Orders thyroid function to exclude thyrotoxicosis

learning_objectives: Apply CHA₂DS₂-VASc scoring for stroke risk stratification per CSANZ AF Guidelines
Select appropriate anticoagulation based on Australian PBS criteria
Implement rate control strategy per eTG Cardiovascular recommendations
Consider rhythm vs rate control decision-making in new-onset AF
references: National Stroke Foundation: Anticoagulation for AF 2021

osces.title: Acute Pericarditis - ECG Interpretation and Management

patient_scenario.chief_complaint: Sharp central chest pain for 3 days, worse with breathing
patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Three-day history of sharp, pleuritic central chest pain. Pain is 7/10 severity, sharp/stabbing quality, worse with deep inspiration and lying flat, improved by sitting forward. No radiation. Associated with low-grade fever and mild dyspnoea. Had upper respiratory tract infection 10 days ago with cough and rhinorrhoea, now resolved. No recent travel, no TB contacts.

social_history.exercise: Gym 3 times weekly, currently unable due to pain
social_history.occupation_detail: Software developer, sedentary work, no occupational exposures

patient_scenario.family_history: Nil cardiac history, mother has SLE

examination_findings.cardiovascular: Pericardial friction rub heard at left sternal edge with patient leaning forward, loudest in expiration. Regular rhythm, normal heart sounds, JVP not elevated, no pulsus paradoxus, no peripheral oedema
examination_findings.respiratory: Clear lung fields bilaterally, no pleural rub
examination_findings.other_systems: No lymphadenopathy, no joint swelling or rash

investigations.ecg: Widespread concave ST elevation in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, V3-V6 measuring 2mm, PR segment depression in leads II and V3-V6, PR elevation in aVR, no reciprocal ST depression, normal QRS morphology
investigations.chest_xray: Normal cardiac silhouette, clear lung fields, no pleural effusion
investigations.bloods: Troponin I 85 ng/L (normal <26, mild elevation common in pericarditis), CRP 68 mg/L (normal <5), ESR 45 mm/hr, WCC 11.8 x10⁹/L with neutrophilia, Creatinine 68 μmol/L, ANA negative, Anti-dsDNA negative
investigations.echocardiogram: Normal LV systolic function, trivial pericardial effusion (<5mm), no tamponade features, no regional wall motion abnormalities

immediate: Ibuprofen 600mg TDS with food for 1-2 weeks (PBS 1896L)
Colchicine 500 micrograms BD for 3 months (PBS 2168Q)
Omeprazole 20mg daily for gastric protection while on NSAIDs (PBS 8225T)
Rest and avoid strenuous exercise until symptoms resolve
Serial ECGs to monitor evolution
short_term: Repeat troponin in 6 hours to ensure no significant rise
Repeat echo in 1 week if symptoms persist
Monitor for complications (effusion, tamponade)
Taper ibuprofen after 1-2 weeks based on symptoms
Continue colchicine for full 3 months to prevent recurrence
long_term: Gradual return to exercise after symptom resolution
Monitor for recurrent pericarditis (15-30% risk)
Consider further investigation if recurrent
Annual follow-up for first year
Education about warning signs of complications
discharge_planning: Return if worsening dyspnoea, fever >38.5°C, or syncope

marking_criteria.item: Identifies widespread ST elevation on ECG
Notes PR depression as pericarditis feature
Differentiates from STEMI (no reciprocal changes, widespread distribution)
Orders echocardiogram to assess for effusion
Checks for secondary causes (ANA, viral serology)

learning_objectives: Recognise ECG features of acute pericarditis per eTG Cardiovascular
Differentiate pericarditis from STEMI using ECG criteria
Prescribe appropriate anti-inflammatory therapy per CSANZ recommendations
Understand role of colchicine in preventing recurrent pericarditis
references: European Society of Cardiology Pericardial Disease Guidelines 2015

osces.title: Stable Angina - Optimal Medical Therapy Initiation

patient_scenario.history_presenting_illness: Six-week history of central chest tightness occurring with exertion. Pain is 6/10 severity, pressure-like quality, occurs after walking 200m on flat ground or climbing one flight of stairs. Radiates to left arm occasionally. Relieved by rest within 5 minutes. No rest pain, no nocturnal symptoms. Episodes becoming more frequent, now daily. Has been avoiding physical activity. No associated dyspnoea, palpitations or syncope.

social_history.exercise: Physical job, no formal exercise due to knee pain
social_history.occupation_detail: Self-employed plumber, heavy lifting, crawling in confined spaces

patient_scenario.family_history: Father had MI age 58, brother has diabetes and hypertension

examination_findings.cardiovascular: Regular rhythm, normal heart sounds, no murmurs, JVP not elevated, peripheral pulses present and equal, no peripheral oedema
examination_findings.other_systems: BMI 29, central adiposity, bilateral knee crepitus, no xanthomata or xanthelasma

investigations.ecg: Sinus rhythm 76 bpm, normal axis, no Q waves, T wave flattening in lateral leads, no acute ST changes
investigations.chest_xray: Normal cardiac size, clear lung fields
investigations.bloods: Troponin I 8 ng/L (normal <26), Total cholesterol 6.2 mmol/L, LDL 4.1 mmol/L, HDL 0.9 mmol/L, Triglycerides 3.8 mmol/L, HbA1c 5.9%, Creatinine 88 μmol/L, eGFR 82 mL/min/1.73m²
investigations.echocardiogram: Normal LV systolic function (LVEF 60%), no regional wall motion abnormalities at rest, mild concentric LVH
investigations.other: Exercise stress test scheduled (or CT coronary angiography)

immediate: Aspirin 100mg daily (PBS 1615Y)
Atorvastatin 40mg nocte (PBS 8242M)
Metoprolol 50mg BD (PBS 2933E)
GTN spray 400 micrograms SL PRN for angina (PBS 8792W)
Education on GTN use: sit down, 1-2 sprays under tongue, repeat after 5 min if needed, call 000 if pain persists after 10 min
short_term: Exercise stress test or CT coronary angiography within 2 weeks
Titrate metoprolol to resting HR 55-60 bpm
Add amlodipine 5mg if angina persists despite beta-blocker
Cardiac rehabilitation referral
Dietitian referral for Mediterranean diet education
long_term: Consider coronary angiography if medical therapy fails
Annual lipid profile with LDL target <1.8 mmol/L
BP target <130/80 mmHg
Weight loss target BMI <25
Smoking cessation maintenance support
Consider SGLT2 inhibitor for additional cardiovascular protection
discharge_planning: Atorvastatin 40mg nocte (increase to 80mg if LDL not at target)
GTN spray PRN with action plan
Cardiology outpatient follow-up in 4 weeks with stress test results
GP follow-up in 1 week for medication tolerance

marking_criteria.item: Prescribes beta-blocker for symptoms and prognosis
Provides GTN spray with appropriate education
Calculates cardiovascular risk and LDL target

learning_objectives: Initiate guideline-directed medical therapy for stable angina per eTG Cardiovascular
Prescribe complete optimal medical therapy per CSANZ Chronic Coronary Syndrome Guidelines
Educate patient on GTN use and angina action plan per National Heart Foundation
Implement comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction strategies
references: CSANZ Guidelines for Chronic Coronary Syndromes 2020
National Heart Foundation: Secondary Prevention of Coronary Heart Disease 2021
PBS Authority Requirements for Cardiovascular Medications 2024
